purpose: Persist the owner thesis: most AI-generated application code is re-generation of already-known primitives, loops, data structures, adapters, logging, and execution patterns. Teleon should let users define capability + context + guardrails, then assemble registered primitives into a verified graph instead of spending tokens rewriting solved code.

essence.claim: Future AI programming should mostly organize proven primitives and abstractions by input/output contract, not write fresh code from scratch.
essence.token_thesis: The model output should shrink from large source-code dumps to compact graph plans such as Input -> Primitive A -> Primitive B -> Primitive C -> Output.
essence.developer_experience: The user defines a capability and the surrounding context. Teleon searches primitive registries, selects compatible blocks, connects edges, verifies contracts, runs, logs, tunes, and stores versions.
essence.why_it_matters: 99% of ordinary loops, structures, retries, scrapers, JSON logs, adapters, transforms, and control patterns have already been solved. Regenerating them wastes tokens and increases defects.

assembly_loop.rule: Capture capability, domain context, input surfaces, output surfaces, guardrails, success metrics, infrastructure constraints, and privacy/license limits before selecting primitives.
Search primitive registries by semantic text, exact contract fields, tags, graph neighborhood, proof history, cost/latency, and license/deployment constraints.
Plan with primitive input/output contracts first. The generated plan should be a graph of primitive calls and adapters, not full rewritten primitive source.
Most novel work should be edge adaptation: mapping outputs to inputs, validating shapes, adding retry/cache/rate-limit policies, and wiring execution surfaces.
Only generate fresh code when no primitive exists or when an adapter/glue layer is strictly needed. New code starts candidate-only and follows the Teleon generated-code contract.
Every run emits structured JSON logs: primitive ids, graph version, input contract hash, output contract hash, timings, costs, errors, retries, and proof status.
Optimization may replace primitives, change order, lower model cost, add batching, or tune retries only if guardrails and success metrics remain satisfied.
Baseline graph, tuned graph variants, forks, regressions, and promoted versions are stored as a versioned graph repository with diffs and rollback.
A newly generated primitive enters the global/private library only after deterministic proofs, contract checks, execution evidence, license metadata, and owner/human approval where needed.

generated_output_policy.preferred_output: A compact capability graph plan plus contract references.
generated_output_policy.avoid: Large regenerated source for primitives that already exist in the registry.

teleon_codegen_relationship.principle: Generated code should be born as candidate primitives or adapters with long meaningful names, purpose/input/output metadata, scalar-or-sequence flexibility, bounded loops, and proof-before-promotion.

external_api_policy.allowed: Third-party APIs can be primitives or execution surfaces.
external_api_policy.requirement: Each external primitive must expose the same contract envelope: input, output, cost, dependency, privacy, license, failure modes, and local/self-hosted fallback when available.
external_api_policy.customer_preference: Some users will prefer installable/integratable code over many external APIs; Teleon should model both as interchangeable primitive implementations behind the same contract.

benefits: Lower token use because models emit graph plans and adapter deltas instead of full primitive source.
Lower defect rate because proven primitives retain tests, logs, contracts, and known failure modes.
Better blast-radius analysis because every primitive and edge is addressable in the graph.
Better tuning because variants can be compared by cost, latency, success rate, and guardrail pass rate.
Better reuse because new verified primitives can be promoted into private or public registries.
Better customer fit because primitives can be local code, private services, or third-party APIs under the same contract.
must_not: Do not treat LLM-authored source as truth.
Do not regenerate a primitive when a verified primitive satisfies the input/output contract.
Do not optimize by breaking declared guardrails.
Do not promote a primitive without proof evidence and license/dependency metadata.
Do not hide external API dependency, cost, privacy, or failure-mode metadata.
